abstract: We construct quantitative negative subspaces for the complete geometric Weil form from hypothetical zeros off the critical line. For zeta and each fixed real primitive Dirichlet character of conductor $q$, put $d=e^{2L}/q$ and $\mathcal H(v)=\pi(\sqrt{4-v^2}-v\arccos(v/2))$. If $20\le Y\le4\pi d-C_\chi$ and $d\mathcal H(Y/(2\pi d))\ge C_\chi J$, where $J=(1+L)^2+\log(Y+2)\log(e/\eta_0)$, every collection of $k$ height-separated actual off-line zero clusters of displacement at least $\eta_0$ gives a $k$-dimensional smooth negative subspace in each parity. Every quotient is at most $-\exp[-4\pi d+2d\mathcal H(Y/(2\pi d))-C_\chi J]$. A greedy selection gives a multiplicity-counting lower bound on the complete negative spectral count. The new analytic input is a uniform lower bound on entire cluster contours for the published complex-pinned equilibrium product. We combine it with whole-cluster interpolation, one common smoothing factor and complete zero-tail and norm estimates for every linear combination. No simplicity or separation inside a cluster is required. For fixed displacement the sufficient radius is $e^{2L}/q=Y/(4\pi)+O_\chi(Y^{1/3}\log^{4/3}Y)$, compared with the earlier leading $Y/(2\pi)$ radius and its different margin guarantees. The proof is analytic; a small CPU control checks finite smoothing values and exact mock interpolation. These are sufficient detection bounds, not optimal crossing laws. No positivity certificate, actual off-line zero, unconditional zero-free region or resolution of RH follows.

coauthors.contribution: Developed the equilibrium-product construction, contributed to the unconditional complex-pinning input and contour-transfer discussion, and checked the complete proof by hand in the preceding joint draft.
